walkthroughs.body_html:
Sources of Wisdom & Authority — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sources of Wisdom & Authority brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sources of Wisdom & Authority.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between act and rule utilitarianism?
options: Act and rule utilitarianism are basically the same approach.
Hinduism worships no gods, only ancestors.
Act utilitarianism is about action movies and rule utilitarianism is about laws.

Act utilitarianism judges each individual action by its consequences; rule utilitarianism follows rules that, if generally adopted, would produce the most good — sacrificing case-by-case calculation for predictability and fairness.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological argument try to prove?
options: The cosmological argument proves who created life on Earth.
The cosmological argument proves the Big Bang happened.
Hinduism worships no gods, only ancestors.
That the existence of the universe requires a first cause or necessary being — usually identified with God — to explain why anything exists at all.
